title: Dynamics 365 Business Central: design custom AI agents with the AI development toolkit
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, preview restrictions, billing description and actionable controls are supported. One minor correction should replace the data-movement control's unconfirmed-applicability caveat with Microsoft's documented scope.

claims.claim: Business Central provides an in-product designer for custom AI agents.

claims.quote: The Create agent wizard allows you to configure your agent by setting up its instructions, profile, and permissions.

claims.claim: Agent instructions are written in natural language.
claims.quote: Instructions are natural language descriptions that define your agent's purpose and behavior.

claims.claim: The designer assigns a profile to an agent.
claims.quote: Under Profile (role), use the Setup profile option to select the profile that determines what UI elements the agent can see and interact with.

claims.claim: The designer assigns permissions to an agent.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The in-product toolkit is available only in sandbox environments, not production.
claims.quote: Sandbox only: Available exclusively in sandbox environments; never in production

claims.claim: The toolkit requires a sandbox from version 27.2.
claims.quote: A sandbox environment for testing and experimentation from version 27.2

claims.claim: Learn targets product owners, domain experts, consultants and developers prototyping AI capabilities.
claims.quote: Product owners who want to prototype AI-powered features before building them in AL extensions; Domain experts; Consultants; Developers

claims.claim: English is currently the only supported language.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: A newly created agent starts in the Disabled state.
claims.quote: An agent is by default in the Disabled state.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Scope
claims.claim: An agent must be activated before it can be used.
claims.quote: You must activate the agent to use it, but you can only activate it after you have defined its purpose and tasks.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Business Central models an agent as a user with permission sets.
claims.quote: The agent is considered as a user in Business Central, so it can be assigned permission sets to control what data and actions it can access.

claims.claim: The roadmap says custom agents extend the runtime used by built-in Sales Order and Payables agents.
claims.quote: extending the same agent runtime capabilities used by built-in Business Central agents.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes import and export of agent definitions as JSON files.
claims.quote: These definitions are stored as simple JSON files containing properties such as agent identity, instructions, assigned profiles, and permissions.

claims.claim: Learn instead describes exported definitions as XML files.
claims.quote: The exported agent appears in your Downloads window in .xml format.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap says custom agents have no built-in email, event or recurring scheduled triggers yet.
claims.quote: there aren't yet any built-in integrations to automatically trigger these custom agents based on incoming emails, events, or scheduled recurrences

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap says professional developers can implement automatic triggers using toolkit APIs.
claims.quote: this can be done by professional developers using the APIs available in the AI Development Toolkit

claims.quote: "status": "In development", "targetDate": "October CY2026"

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Custom agent runs consume Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: These capabilities use Copilot Credits for AI interactions and tasks ... Billable agent capabilities ... Designing and coding agents (preview)

claims.claim: Learn says agents cannot have more permissions than their creating user.
claims.quote: Permission inheritance: Agents can't have more permissions than their creating user

claims.claim: A scheduled task uses the intersection of the scheduling user's and agent's permissions.
claims.quote: When a user schedules a task for an agent, the task is executed with permissions from the intersection of the user's permissions and the agent's permissions.

claims.claim: The transparency note instead describes permission intersection with the task approver.
claims.quote: It then runs with the intersection of the permissions given to the agent with the permissions of the user that approved the task

claims.claim: The transparency note uses the configurator's permissions when task approval was not required.
claims.quote: or the user that configured the agent, if task approval wasn't required.

claims.claim: After user intervention, a task continues with the responding user's permissions.
claims.quote: If the agent makes a user intervention request, the task continues proceeding with the permissions of the user that responded to that intervention request.

claims.claim: The intervention responder may differ from the task creator.
claims.quote: This user might be different from the task creator.

claims.claim: Variable is the applicable cost category because agent capabilities are metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are the billing units that measure usage.

claims.claim: The cross-geography processing control is Business Central > Copilot & agent capabilities > Allow data movement toggle.
claims.quote: enter Copilot & agent capabilities, and then choose the related link. Switch the Allow data movement toggle on or off as desired.

claims.claim: Learn documents no administrator API for the Business Central Allow data movement toggle.
claims.quote: Searched: Business Central Allow data movement API PowerShell AL setting; Allow data movement codeunit API; Copilot AI Capabilities data movement table API. Opened enable-ai, ai-copilot-data-movement and Copilot Capability reference; no operation setting this toggle found.

claims.claim: The Allow data movement toggle appears only when cross-geography processing is relevant.
claims.quote: The Allow data movement toggle appears when one or more copilot and agent capabilities might process data in a different Azure geography from the Business Central environment.

claims.claim: The correctly documented general data-movement control is presented with a caveat that Learn does not confirm applicability to Custom Agent.
claims.quote: The Allow data movement setting ... applies to geographic processing for Business Central Copilot and agent capabilities that use Microsoft-managed AI resources through Business Central.
claims.fix: Replace 'Learn does not say it applies to Custom Agent' in the row note and rendered table with 'Applies to geographic processing for Business Central Copilot and agent capabilities that use Microsoft-managed AI resources through Business Central.' Remove the corresponding applicability question from Open questions; cite https://learn.microsoft.com/dynamics365/business-central/enable-ai.

claims.claim: Capacity allocation is reached at Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Prepaid capacity > Manage Capacity > environment > Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Select the Summary tab ... Select Manage Capacity from the Prepaid capacity card ... In the allocation panel, select an environment and specify the number of Copilot Credits to allocate in the Copilot Credits textbox.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 writes an environment's credit allocation.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com"; $apiVersion = "2024-10-01"; Invoke-RestMethod -Method Put -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=$apiVersion"

claims.claim: The allocation request identifies its environment through scope.environmentId.
claims.quote: scope = @{ environmentId = $environmentId }

claims.claim: allocatedEntitlements[].entitlementId uses MCSMessages for Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are represented by the entitlement ID MCSMessages ... allocatedEntitlements = @( @{ entitlementId = "MCSMessages"

claims.claim: allocatedEntitlements[].allocation.quantity sets the credit allocation amount.
claims.quote: allocatedEntitlements = @( @{ entitlementId = "MCSMessages"; allocation = @{ quantity = 5000 }

claims.claim: The allocation API requires a Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or equivalent capacity-management role.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator or Global Administrator role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: Allocating capacity to a linked Power Platform environment governs its Business Central environment's credit consumption.
claims.quote: Once completed, consumption of the Copilot Credits in the Business Central environment is limited by the capacity allocated to the linked Power Platform environment.

claims.claim: Only internal admins can link a Business Central environment to a Power Platform environment.
claims.quote: Link the Business Central environment to the Power Platform environment. Only internal admins can complete this task.

claims.claim: Capability changes may take effect immediately or require users to sign out and back in.
claims.quote: Some AI features take effect immediately, while others require users to sign out and sign in again.

claims.claim: The TenantPool enforcement rule maps to Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote: The Draw from the available capacity in my tenant option in the admin center maps to the TenantPool enforcement rule

claims.claim: An enabled TenantPool rule allows use of unallocated tenant capacity after the environment allocation is exhausted.
claims.quote: when it's enabled, the environment continues to draw from unallocated tenant capacity after its own allocation is exhausted

claims.claim: The allocation tutorial describes a disabled TenantPool rule as capping the environment at its allocation.

claims.where: Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Both tenant-pool draw and pay-as-you-go overage must be cleared to restrict consumption to allocated prepaid credits.
claims.quote: Draw from the available capacity in my tenant ... Bill to my pay-as-you-go billing plan ... If no overage source is enabled, the environment can consume only its allocated prepaid credits.

claims.claim: An environment-group rule governing tenant-pool draw blocks individual changes with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy.
claims.quote: If a published environment group rule governs Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, you can't override the setting for an individual environment ... rejected with the TenantPoolLockedByPolicy error.

claims.claim: The roadmap recommends keeping exported agent definition files in source control.
claims.quote: We recommend storing these files in a source control system like GitHub to track changes and maintain version history.
